access_key.description: Access Key required to communicate with Binocs API. Get yours at [https://binocs.sh](https://binocs.sh)

secret_key.description: Secret Key required to communicate with Binocs API. Get yours at [https://binocs.sh](https://binocs.sh)

alias.description: The alias (name) of this notification channel. Maximum length is 25 characters.

checks.description: The checks to associate with this notifications channel.

handle.description: The e-mail address for a channel of `type = email`.

type.description: The only supported channel is currently "email", and it requires e-mail address verification. All other notification channels (telegram, slack) currently require interactive creation using Binocs CLI. All notification channels can be imported to Terraform.

down_confirmations_threshold.description: How many subsequent "down" responses need to occur before Binocs closes an incident and triggers "recovery" notifications. Minimum is 1 and maximum is 10.

interval.description: How often Binocs checks this resource, in seconds. Minimum is 5 and maximum is 900 seconds.

method.description: The HTTP method (one of GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE). Only used and required with HTTP(S) resources.

name.description: The name (alias) of this check. Maximum length is 25 characters.

regions.description: From where in the world Binocs checks this resource. At least one region is required. Valid values: af-south-1, ap-east-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, sa-east-1, us-east-1, us-west-1.

resource.description: The resource to check; a valid URL in case of a HTTP(S) resource, or tcp://{HOSTNAME}:{PORT} in case of a TCP resource.

target.description: The response time that accommodates Apdex=1.0 (in seconds with up to 3 decimal places). Valid target is a value between 0.01 and 10.0 seconds.

up_codes.description: The good ("up") HTTP(S) response codes, e.g. 2xx or `200-302`, or `200,301`. Only used with HTTP(S) resources.

up_confirmations_threshold.description: How many subsequent "up" responses need to occur before Binocs creates an incident and triggers notifications. Minimum is 1 and maximum is 10.
